column1: # acmg_sf.tsv: the ACMG SF v3.3 secondary-findings genes and the reporting rule of each
# (bin/collect_summary.py acmg_sf_tier). One row per gene, 84 rows. Source: Lee et al., ACMG SF v3.3
# list for reporting of secondary findings in clinical exome and genome sequencing, Genet Med
# 2026-10-27. HGNC ids from rest.genenames.org on 2026-10-27; GRCh38 positions from Ensembl.
#   gene, hgnc_id   the HGNC symbol and id
#   inheritance     AD, AR, SD (semidominant) or XL, as Table 1 gives it
#   report_if       when a P/LP variant (ClinVar, or a rare HIGH-impact record) is a secondary finding:
#                     biallelic       two variants: a homozygote, or two different variants even when
#                                     their phase is unknown (Table 1 footnote a)
#                     hom_variant     only a variant of the variants column, homozygous
#                     hemizygous      a hemizygous or homozygous variant, or two heterozygous ones; a
#                                     single heterozygous variant is not reported
#                     het_female_too  any variant, heterozygous females included
#   variants        report_if hom_variant: the only variants that count, as chrom:pos:ref:alt (GRCh38)
#                   and a name; "." for every other gene
#   sv_cn           yes: an AnnotSV class 4 or 5 structural variant or copy change over the gene is a
#                   finding too (step 05); no: small variants only
#   sv_regions      other regions whose class 4 or 5 deletion counts for this gene, as chrom:start-end
#   severity        alleles that do not count as a full loss of function, separated by ";": each is
#                   hypomorph or pseudodeficiency, then chrom:pos:ref:alt, then a name. A
#                   pseudodeficiency allele is set aside; a hypomorph allele counts, but the finding says
#   sf_version      the ACMG SF list version that added the gene (Table 1)
#   note            what Table 1's footnotes add, shown with the finding; "."
